mechanism: Discretize price into fixed-size blocks (from M1 closes); for windows of N steps count vertical block amplitude; compare the empirical amplitude histogram to a combinatorial 50%-reversal reference. Markets whose distribution is wider/lower than the reference have P(continuation)>0.5 (trend regime); trendiness weakens as block scale grows.
data_needed: M1 closes; block size N points; many samples of N-step vertical amplitudes; reference histogram for 50% random walk.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AMD, AAPL, TSLA, SBER, AMEZ stocks; EURUSD; ~30 FX pairs, cryptos, commodities; block scales from 1 pt to thousands; robot on M1 real ticks 2018–2020.
why_new_for_mis: Gives a scale-dependent trend-vs-flat regime score from block-amplitude distributions vs an explicit random-walk null, not from MA slope or ADX.
quote: the analyzed chart has a trend continuation probability above 50%, and thus the stock is likely to continue the trend.

mechanism: Set block size = k * ATR (current or higher TF) so the discrete sensor rescale with volatility; optionally size lots as lot_set/(BS/min_BS) to keep risk stable as blocks grow.
data_needed: ATR on working or higher TF; coefficient k; min block size; lot settings.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, AAPL, AMD, TSLA, SBER; M1 blocks; dynamic ATR block sizing in tests.
why_new_for_mis: Couples the trendiness block sensor’s resolution and risk to live ATR so MIS can keep regime features comparable across vol regimes.
quote: with an increase in volatility, the block size will grow and the system will adapt to changing market parameters.

mechanism: Hypothesis: money issuance / investment attractiveness raises trendiness; high liquidity and smart participants raise entropy and cut trendiness. Empirically maps instruments (EURUSD ~1.068, AAPL ~1.3, SBER ~1.168, AMEZ <1 flat) as a cross-asset regime prior.
data_needed: Per-symbol trendiness ratio from block distributions; liquidity/participation proxies.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, AAPL, SBER, AMEZ; multiple block scales.
why_new_for_mis: Turns instrument class (attractiveness vs liquidity) into a prior on expected trend regime usable for MIS universe selection.
quote: high investment attractiveness increases the degree of trendiness, and high liquidity and a large number of participants reduce the degree of trade

mechanism: Discretize price by fixed H-point steps; build empirical P(s) of net up-steps over n steps vs combinatorial null C(n,u)/2^n. Beta K=Sum(P[i]*|s[i]|) vs KMid of null → trend% if K>KMid else flat%; Alpha T=Sum(P[i]*s[i]) → signed bull/bear%. Live indicator overlays current vs neutral density.
data_needed: Step size in points; n formula steps; rolling step memory; combinatorial reference arrays.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any FX chart; indicator inputs BarsI, StepsMemory, StepsI, StepPoints; examples with n=20/51/100.
why_new_for_mis: Quantifies simultaneous directional (alpha) and non-directional continuation (beta) regimes against an exact combinatorial null—usable as a dual-axis regime sensor.
quote: If Кp > K, the market can be considered trending. If Кp < K, the market is flat.

mechanism: Four Sequential stages mark equilibrium breaks: (1) start/breakout close more extreme than close 4 bars back; (2) 9-bar Setup streak; (3) Intersection/crossover rectangle; (4) Countdown to 13 comparing close vs high/low 2 bars back. Each stage is an imbalance zone that can pivot or act as S/R.
data_needed: OHLC; Setup_Distance=4, Setup_Limit=9, Intersection_Min_Distance, Countdown_Distance=2, Countdown_Limit=13.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD H4/W1; SP500 H1; multi-TF top-down suggested; MetaQuotes-Demo GMT+3.
why_new_for_mis: Stages a multi-phase imbalance/regime-change timeline rather than a single oscillator cross—MIS can treat Setup star, Intersection box, and Countdown arrow as distinct change sensors.
quote: imbalance points (or areas): (а) indicate a possible trend change and (b) represent strong support/resistance zones for further movements.

mechanism: Anchor Murray-Gann 1/8 grids on Sequential extrema (breakout candle, Intersection high/low, signal candle); expand range when +2/8 breaks; read price location in 0/8–8/8 (and ±1/8,±2/8) as precise ‘where in range’ state, with 6/8 and 4/8 as stronger mid levels.
data_needed: Chosen Sequential extrema as base points; Murray octave levels; optional Fibo 0.125 grid.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD H4/W1 examples; works with any level indicator answering ‘where exactly up/down’.
why_new_for_mis: Fuses event-driven Sequential anchors with octave range geometry into a position-in-structure sensor finer than raw trend/flat labels.
quote: they answer the questions "where exactly up" or "where exactly down".

mechanism: Long-run bullish≈bearish candle counts (~50%). Scan windows [MinBars,MaxBars] for local excess OpenPerc of one color; fade excess (buy if bearish dominate, sell if bullish); size series length from expected return-to-50% candles R=(N+NB-NM)*K; close when excess ≤ ClosePerc or profit-per-lot hit.
data_needed: Close-direction candles; MinBars/MaxBars/Step; OpenPerc/ClosePerc; K; CloseProfit.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD/EURUSD/GBPJPY H1/M15/H4; GAZP/AAPL M15 stats; backtests to ~2000–2020.
why_new_for_mis: Uses signed candle-count imbalance vs a universal 50% equilibrium—and its instrument-specific reversion speed—as the primary regime-change trigger.
quote: when a deviation from the equilibrium occurs, the rate of return to the equilibrium for each instrument is individual, stable and fluctuates within certain limits.

mechanism: Replace fixed OpenPerc with a rarity-matched nonlinear threshold: P=2*C(n,k)/2^n for excess events; fit %excess(n) so occurrence probability stays ~constant as n grows (Koef_NonLiner_proc). Also weighted-average % and multi-sample counts across [Min_diap_bar,Max_diap_bar] to fuzzy the analysis window.
data_needed: Candle counts per sample size; combinatorial probability table; Koef_NonLiner_proc; Kol_vibor; Porog_Weighted_proc.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD/EURUSD/GBPJPY H1/M15; 28 FX majors; windows e.g. 68–200 bars, 15 samples.
why_new_for_mis: Makes imbalance detection scale-invariant by holding combinatorial rarity fixed—MIS can compare excesses across window lengths fairly.
quote: combinations for 30 candles with the bullish/bearish candle excess of 80% occur as often as combinations of 100 candles with the excess of 66%.

mechanism: CloseProfit in points = ATR(points)*Koef_multi_ATR (avg points from open across series); lot = NormLot / (ATR/Norm_ATR) so higher vol → smaller lot, flattening equity. Optional min-ATR gate to skip low-vol regimes.
data_needed: ATR; Koef_multi_ATR; Norm_ATR/Norm lot; optional min ATR.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD H1 2000–2020 dynamic-lot test; 28 pairs multi-symbol.
why_new_for_mis: Converts ATR into both exit distance and position-scale sensors so MIS vol state directly modulates trade geometry.
quote: To stabilize the profitability graph, we need to change the lot size based on the current volatility.

mechanism: Build fixed-point blocks from M1; Max_distribution measures mean vertical blocks in N steps across block sizes; compare to combinatorial RW reference (e.g. 3.868 for 24 steps). Amplitude >> reference ⇒ trend-like; near/below ⇒ flat-like; multi-N curves describe scale structure. Rollback depth inferred from how amplitude must return toward its mean at larger step counts.
data_needed: M1→blocks; min block size & growth factor; N-step samples (e.g. 1000); reference table.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: ~35 FX, 100+ stocks, 10 cryptos, ~10 commodities; GBPUSD examples; synthetic sinewave calibration.
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes trend/flat per scale via measured mean path amplitude vs RW null, plus rollback geometry from amplitude conservation—core multi-scale regime sensing.
quote: the market should always have a scale currently showing a flat (the reversal probability is higher than the trend continuation one) and a scale currently showing a trend

mechanism: Scan block-‘timeframes’ grown by KTF (e.g. 1.1) over analysis range (e.g. 24–28 blocks); promote the largest TF still above probability-table %open to basic TF; delay entry until higher TF cannot form (statistical Nd/Nbd delay using %open and block sizes); TP/close % from expected rollback vs amplitude. Skips pure flat (no scale trends) and endless trends (TF keeps growing).
data_needed: Min block from ATR*ratio & costs; KTF; Nb range; probability→%open/%close tables; Ka/Kc amplitude multipliers.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Designed for any FX/exchange symbol; M1 base; synthetic sinewave demos.
why_new_for_mis: Live adaptive finder of the maximum active trend scale with a statistically timed ‘trend-over’ gate—MIS regime scale + change confirmation in one loop.
quote: the task is to find the maximum timeframe, on which there is a signal for the beginning of the series, and make it basic.

mechanism: When parent series basic TF exceeds threshold, spawn child series only if child finds local imbalance AND a flat segment on child basic TF within Bmin–Bmax (Bmin=NPb/(%PV/100); Bmax from blocks inside last two parent blocks), with flat % from probability tables—ensuring child trades nested flat inside parent trend.
data_needed: Parent/child block TFs; NPb; %PV; Bmin/Bmax; confirmation probability table.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD 2008 long-trend example; 28 FX M1 2008–2021; AAPL; 28 MOEX names.
why_new_for_mis: Senses nested flat-within-trend structure to authorize multi-scale concurrent regimes instead of a single global label.
quote: make sure that the found trend area is a part of the flat area, rather than of a large trend used for the first series operation.

mechanism: Convert each symbol’s bars to USD P&L path for fixed notional (pair-type formulas); observe that trends on some pairs coincide with flats on others (~$2.26*sqrt(N) mean vertical). Route 80% of first-series profits across the book to heal erroneous positions—portfolio-level complementary regime sensor.
data_needed: 28+ symbols’ OHLC; USD-notional candle sizes; shared compensation pool.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 28 FX majors/crosses M1 2008–2021; 28 MOEX stocks; AAPL long/short; GBPUSD+AUDNZD+EURCAD+CHFJPY demo.
why_new_for_mis: Elevates MIS from single-symbol regime to cross-sectional complementarity of trend/flat across a multi-market book.
quote: a flat is detected on some currency pairs during a trend on others.

mechanism: Time-filter labels to one hour or weekday; train CatBoost (+GMM synthetic) repeatedly; scatter R² by hour/day. Dense high-R² clusters (e.g. hours 3–6, Friday) mark stable seasonal tradability regimes; high-dispersion hours mark unstable time slots. Also sweep deal lifetime bars for horizon sensitivity.
data_needed: H1 OHLC with datetime index; hour/dow filters; GMM; CatBoost brute-force iterations.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD H1; train from 2017, test from 2015; long history to 1990/2000; hours 0–23, weekdays 0–4; horizons 1–50 bars.
why_new_for_mis: Treats clock/calendar slots as measurable regime dimensions via stability of ML R² density, not fixed session dummies.
quote: passes for hours 4, 5 and 6 hours are located more closely, which gives more confidence in the quality of the found pattern.

mechanism: Couple base CatBoost (direction) with meta CatBoost (trade/skip). Iteratively: test pair, label meta 1/0 by trade P&L, drop base samples meta rejects, accumulate BAD_SAMPLES_BOOK of recurrent failure timestamps (keep those above mean*fraction as forced zeros). Meta gates live trading—auto timing that skips hard-to-classify segments.
data_needed: Features (e.g. close−MA windows); labels; meta_labels; BAD_SAMPLES_BOOK; START/TSTART/STOP date splits.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD and GBPJPY H1; MA periods 15–500; horizons 15–35; history from ~2010; 25 training iterations.
why_new_for_mis: Learns a sequence/timing sensor of when patterns are present vs absent, raising precision by filtering Class-I false trades without hand-built session rules.
quote: sort out the parts of the time series that are difficult to classify and skip them during training and trading

mechanism: modAL uncertainty/batch/committee active learning + GMM resampling into CatBoost; improves sample efficiency of classifiers but builds no market regime/vol/liquidity sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Unspecified FX features; 1y train / 5y test charts in figures.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: ML labeling methodology only—no new MIS market-state sense.
quote: I have not seen any significant increase in the quality of the models.

mechanism: In a sliding horizon, simulate buy and sell grids (distances, lot coefficients/martingale); label the side with max total triggered-order profit>0. CatBoost then predicts grid-favorable direction—implicit sensor of paths where multi-level mean-reversion grids pay.
data_needed: Close path over horizon; GRID_SIZE/DISTANCES/COEFFICIENTS; MARKUP.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train ~2020-05→2022; eval from 2019/2018; stress from 2015; aggressive linspace lots 1..5.
why_new_for_mis: Relabels ‘good market state’ as aggregate grid P&L geometry rather than single mid-price direction—useful MIS target for oscillation/grid-friendly regimes.
quote: it is necessary to calculate the total profit for all triggered pending orders including the order opened at the very beginning

mechanism: Explains Sharpe=(Return-RiskFree)/Std and Sortino with downside semi-volatility; annualization by sqrt(bars); equity log-return variant for testers. Evaluation metrics for strategies/portfolios, not a market sensing construct.
data_needed: Asset or equity returns; optional risk-free rate.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY/USDCHF 2020; M1–MN1; MACD Sample Sharpe EA.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: performance-ratio tutorial only—no MIS regime/vol/liquidity/sequence market sensor.
quote: Sharpe and Sortino ratios allow the determining of whether the received profit covers the associated risk or not.
